items.title: Tinengotinib Combined With Standard Treatments for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial tests tinengotinib, a new investigational drug, in combination with standard hormone treatments (abiraterone or enzalutamide) for men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The study aims to determine if this combination is safe and causes only mild side effects. This is an early-phase study that could lead to a new treatment option if results are promising.

items.title: SX-682 Plus Docetaxel for Advanced Prostate Cancer That Has Spread
items.summary: This trial studies SX-682, a new drug that blocks immune cells that help tumors grow, combined with docetaxel chemotherapy. It includes patients with prostate cancer that has returned after treatment or spread to other areas. The study will test safety and effectiveness of this combination in both head/neck cancers and prostate cancer.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial of Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Standard Treatments
items.summary: This major phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig (a new immunotherapy) plus abiraterone against doctor's choice of treatment (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone alone) in patients with mCRPC who have not yet received chemotherapy. The primary goal is to see if the combination helps patients live longer. This is a pivotal trial that could change treatment standards if successful.

items.title: DNA Vaccines With Pembrolizumab for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial tests whether using two DNA vaccines (pTVG-HP and pTVG-AR) together with pembrolizumab immunotherapy works better than one vaccine with pembrolizumab. The study aims to activate the immune system to attack prostate cancer cells more effectively. Treatment lasts up to 2 years with 5 years of follow-up.

items.title: Safety Study of JSB462 (Luxdegalutamide) in Japanese Patients
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety, tolerability, and how the body processes JSB462 (luxdegalutamide), a new hormone therapy drug, specifically in Japanese patients with metastatic prostate cancer. Early-phase safety studies like this are important for understanding how new drugs work in different populations before larger trials begin.

items.title: Lutetium-177 Dotatate for Prostate Cancer With Neuroendocrine Features
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies lutetium Lu 177 dotatate, a radioactive drug therapy, in patients with metastatic prostate cancer that has neuroendocrine features. Some prostate cancers develop neuroendocrine cells that don't respond to standard hormone treatments. This drug targets these cells by delivering radiation directly to them, potentially offering a new treatment option for this aggressive variant.

items.title: REGN5678 (Nezastomig) Alone or With Cemiplimab for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests REGN5678 (nezastomig), a new immunotherapy drug, either alone or combined with cemiplimab (another immunotherapy) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will first find a safe dose, then test how well it shrinks tumors. It also examines how the drugs work in the body and what side effects patients may experience.

items.title: Darolutamide With ADT and Docetaxel for Low-Volume Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This observational study tracks real-world use of darolutamide combined with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and docetaxel chemotherapy in Japanese men with low-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study will collect data from routine medical care to understand safety and effectiveness of this combination therapy in practice, helping doctors make better treatment decisions.

items.title: Enzalutamide Safety Study in Indian Patients With Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed phase 4 study evaluated the safety and tolerability of enzalutamide in Indian patients with progressive mCRPC who had previously received docetaxel chemotherapy. The study also measured effects on PSA levels. Phase 4 studies like this help understand how approved drugs perform in specific populations.

items.title: Radium-223 With M3814 and Avelumab for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial (currently suspended) tests combinations of radium-223 dichloride (radiation therapy injected into the bloodstream) with M3814 (a drug that blocks DNA repair) and/or avelumab (immunotherapy) for castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to bones. The study aims to find the best combination to kill cancer cells while sparing normal tissue.

items.title: Sipuleucel-T With or Without Continuing Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether continuing new hormonal agents (abiraterone, enzalutamide, or apalutamide) during treatment with sipuleucel-T (Provenge) vaccine therapy improves immune system activation in patients with asymptomatic mCRPC without visceral metastases. The study is no longer enrolling but still following participants to see if the combination enhances the vaccine's effectiveness.

items.title: Xaluritamig With Hormone Therapies for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety and tolerability of xaluritamig (an immunotherapy) combined with darolutamide or abiraterone in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. This tests whether adding immunotherapy to standard hormone treatments is safe in earlier-stage metastatic disease, which could expand treatment options if successful.

items.title: AMO959 With Lu-177 PSMA and Hormone Therapy for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1b/2 trial combines AMO959 (an investigational drug) with lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy and an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor in patients with mCRPC who failed one prior hormone therapy. The study will determine safe dosing and evaluate effectiveness in patients who haven't yet received chemotherapy. This represents a novel three-drug combination approach.

items.title: Intermittent Relugolix Plus Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates intermittent (on-and-off) treatment with relugolix combined with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer who achieve good PSA response. Intermittent therapy may reduce side effects while maintaining cancer control, potentially improving quality of life without sacrificing effectiveness.

items.title: AZD9750 With or Without Saruparib for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: ANDROMEDA is a first-in-human phase 1/2 trial testing AZD9750, a completely new investigational drug, either alone or combined with saruparib in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The study will evaluate safety, how the drug works in the body, and early signs of effectiveness. First-in-human trials are critical first steps in developing new treatments.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Plus Luxdegalutamide Versus Standard Care for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: TulmiSTAR-01 is a phase 1/2 trial testing the combination of tulmimetostat (an epigenetic drug) and JSB462/luxdegalutamide (a hormone therapy) compared to standard treatments in patients with progressive mCRPC. The study will first establish safe dosing, then compare effectiveness against standard care. This combination targets cancer through two different mechanisms.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial of Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares mevrometostat (an investigational epigenetic drug) plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who haven't received prior hormone therapy or chemotherapy. This is a pivotal trial that could establish a new first-line treatment combination if the combination proves superior to standard therapy.

items.title: Phase 3 Study of Ifinatamab Deruxtecan for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd or MK-2400), an antibody-drug conjugate that delivers chemotherapy directly to cancer cells, helps patients with mCRPC live longer overall and live longer without cancer progression compared to standard chemotherapy. This is a major trial that could lead to FDA approval of a new treatment.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Combination Therapies for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: KEYNOTE-365 is a large multi-cohort phase 1/2 study testing pembrolizumab (immunotherapy) combined with various drugs including olaparib, docetaxel, enzalutamide, abiraterone, lenvatinib, vibostolimab, carboplatin/etoposide, and belzutifan. The study is no longer enrolling but continues to follow patients to evaluate safety and effectiveness of these different immunotherapy combinations.

items.title: Inflammation Drives Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer Through Multiple Pathways
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation promotes prostate cancer progression and resistance to hormone therapy. It describes how inflammatory signaling pathways (NFκB and JAK/STAT3) work together with androgen receptor signaling to help tumors survive, grow, spread, and evade the immune system. Understanding these mechanisms may lead to new treatment strategies targeting inflammation in castration-resistant disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study shows that a next-generation nanoplasmid DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein highly expressed on prostate cancer cells) can activate the immune system and improve response to PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy. In laboratory studies, the vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastasis, and increased immune system activation when combined with immunotherapy. This could lead to human trials.

items.title: Real-World Use of Comprehensive Genomic Testing in Cancer Patients
items.source: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
items.summary: This Finnish study analyzed how comprehensive genomic profiling was used in 297 cancer patients in routine practice from 2017-2020. Among patients tested, 16.8% had prostate cancer, most had metastatic disease, and were heavily pretreated. About 65% of patients had at least one actionable genetic alteration that could guide treatment decisions. This demonstrates real-world utility of genomic testing.

items.title: Phase 1a Study of Lu-177 PSMA With Capecitabine in Metastatic CRPC
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This phase 1a trial tested lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy combined with capecitabine (an oral chemotherapy drug that may enhance radiation effects) in patients with mCRPC. The study aimed to determine if adding capecitabine as a radiosensitizer could improve the effectiveness of PSMA-targeted radiation therapy. Results from this early safety study could inform larger trials.
